NDT training in Lafayette, LA: how it works

Short answer: Lafayette technicians study NDT theory self-paced on the Atlantis online portal, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, and access starts the moment they enroll. Hands-on practice happens in the Practical NDT browser simulator and in person at the employer's shop or yard. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Lafayette. The employer certifies you under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or you can sit ASNT central exams.

Lafayette grew up as the onshore office and workshop of the Gulf of Mexico oil patch. Drilling contractors, tool makers, machine shops, tubular inspection companies and offshore service firms cluster along the I-10 and US-90 corridors, and many technicians here spend their careers inspecting things that go downhole or offshore. That is a different job from refinery turnaround work in Baton Rouge or Lake Charles, and the training should reflect it: threaded connections, drill pipe, tubing and casing, lifting equipment and welded skids come up far more often than process piping circuits.

The way the training is put together follows from that. You work through the theory on the portal at your own pace, between hitches or after a shift. The practical skill comes from scanning, magnetizing and interpreting on real parts at a Lafayette employer, logged as supervised experience. The certificate that lets you sign a report comes from the employer, not from any course.

Ask about NDT training in Lafayette and tell us your methods, levels and how many people need training. We reply within one business day.

How to get NDT certified in Lafayette: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Most Acadiana service companies certify their own people under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The sequence below is what an auditor or an operator's quality group will expect to see in your file.

  1. Find or confirm the written practice. Your Lafayette employer's written practice sets the training hours, experience hours, examinations and vision checks for each method and level. If you are not yet hired, use the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker to see what a typical program asks for.
  2. Complete formal training. Take the theory for your method and level on the portal. The SNT-TC-1A hours planner shows the recommended minimum hours by method.
  3. Log supervised experience. Work the method on real parts under a certified Level II or Level III, and keep the hours in a log your supervisor signs.
  4. Pass the general examination, which tests the principles, equipment and vocabulary of the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination on your employer's procedures, equipment and acceptance criteria, for example the criteria an operator writes into its tubular inspection specification.
  6. Pass the practical examination on representative specimens, graded under the authority of a Level III.
  7. Pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and color contrast, at the interval the written practice sets.
  8. Receive employer certification. Your employer signs the certification, and it is valid only while you work for that employer.
  9. Recertify at the interval in the written practice; SNT-TC-1A recommends no longer than five years.

Technicians who want a credential that is not tied to one company can prepare for ASNT central certification instead: ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, or the ASNT NDT Level III examinations. Atlantis prepares candidates for those exams as well. Background reading: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Lafayette technicians

Every course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method. The right-hand column shows where each method earns its keep in the Lafayette market. Start with Level 1 NDT training, move to Level 2 NDT training once you have hours, and use ASNT Level III training when you are ready to write procedures and grade exams.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Lafayette
UTSound physics, calibration, straight-beam thickness and lamination checks, angle-beam weld examinationWall-thickness surveys on drill pipe and tubing, end-area inspection, welds on skids, tanks and offshore structures
PAUT and TOFDFocal laws, encoded scanning, setup files, data review and flaw sizing for experienced UT Level II techniciansPipeline and structural welds where the owner's specification allows advanced UT
MTMagnetization methods, field direction, wet fluorescent and visible techniques, demagnetizationThreaded connections, tool joints, rotary shouldered connections, lifting gear and fabricated steel
PTPenetrant process control, dwell, removal, developer and interpretationNon-magnetic drilling components, stainless fittings, valve bodies and machined parts
VTVisual acuity, lighting, gauges, weld and thread visual criteriaThread and shoulder condition, weld visual on every fabrication, receiving inspection of tubulars
RTExposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital imaging, interpretationPipeline girth welds, piping spools and castings for shops that hold a radiography license
ETImpedance-plane basics, probes, calibration and surface or tubing techniquesSurface crack checks on helicopter and aircraft components, heat-exchanger tubing at plants along the corridor

A Level 3 candidate in Lafayette usually already runs a technical department. The Level III course is exam preparation for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations, plus practice writing procedures and examinations, which is what an Acadiana inspection company most needs its Level III to do.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Lafayette

UT is the method most Lafayette technicians add after their surface methods. In tubular and drill-string work it starts with straight-beam thickness readings and lamination checks, then moves to angle-beam examination of welds on fabricated equipment. The ultrasonic testing training course covers calibration on reference blocks, velocity and attenuation, couplant and surface condition on mill-scaled or coated pipe, and how to record readings so an operator can trust them.

The method used most around Lafayette, though, is magnetic particle testing. Thread and connection inspection on drill pipe, heavy-weight pipe, collars and downhole tools leans on wet fluorescent MT under black light, with visual and dimensional checks alongside. Inspection to drill stem standards such as API RP 7G-2 and the industry DS-1 standard combines VT, MT and UT, and operators often specify which category of inspection they want. If your employer does that work, take magnetic particle testing training and visual testing training first, then UT.

Electromagnetic inspection of tubing and casing is also common in Lafayette inspection yards. It is usually run on proprietary equipment under the yard's own procedures, so the employer trains its operators on that equipment directly; a sound UT and MT foundation makes that training much easier to absorb.

Where NDT technicians work around Lafayette

Oilfield services and drilling tools. Lafayette and the neighboring towns of Broussard, Youngsville, Scott and Carencro host the regional bases of many service companies, along with machine shops that cut threads and rebuild tools. They need technicians who can inspect connections, tubulars and rental tools before they go back offshore.

Tubular inspection yards. New and used casing, tubing and drill pipe pass through inspection yards across Acadiana before running. That work mixes VT, MT, UT and electromagnetic inspection, and it is often where new technicians get their first logged hours.

Offshore fabrication and the Port of Iberia. The Port of Iberia near New Iberia, south of Lafayette, is home to fabricators that build modules, skids and structures for offshore and industrial projects. Welds there run to AWS D1.1, ASME Section VIII and API structural requirements, which keeps VT, MT, UT and RT busy.

Helicopter and aviation maintenance. Lafayette is a base for offshore helicopter operations, and PHI Aviation is headquartered in the city. Aircraft maintenance follows FAA requirements and the manufacturers' NDT manuals, mostly ET, PT and MT on components.

Pipelines and gas infrastructure. Henry Hub, the pipeline interconnect at Erath in Vermilion Parish, sits about twenty miles south-west of Lafayette, and gathering and transmission lines cross the parishes around it. Pipeline construction and integrity digs need RT or UT on girth welds to API 1104 and UT thickness on corroded pipe.

For pay information, see the NDT Level 2 salary page, which cites public sources.

NDT schools and classes near Lafayette: what to compare

People in Acadiana searching for an NDT school near them usually choose between a classroom program at a school and self-paced theory followed by practical training at an employer. Both can work. What matters is whether the hours and records will satisfy the written practice of the company that eventually certifies you.

Questions to put to any provider, including us:

  • Which document is the course built on, and does the certificate of completion state the method, level and hours in a form an auditor can check?
  • Who wrote the course, and what Level III certifications does that person hold?
  • How is the practical side handled, and on what equipment and specimens?
  • Does the course prepare you for an employer's general and specific examinations, or for an ASNT central examination, or both?
  • What happens to the training record if you change employer?

Atlantis answers those questions this way: theory self-paced on the portal, questions answered by an ASNT NDT Level III, practice in the browser simulator, hands-on practical work and the practical examination in person at the employer's facility under its written practice. The published US fees are shown on this page, and Register & Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal. More common questions are answered on the NDT training FAQ.

Online NDT training in Louisiana

Online theory suits Louisiana's offshore workforce particularly well, because rotation schedules make fixed class times hard to keep. On the Atlantis portal the theory modules and Level III preparation are self-paced, so you can study on days off and pick up where you left off. Questions go to the Level III through the portal.

What online study cannot do is replace the practical. Louisiana employers, like those anywhere else, certify only after hands-on experience and a practical examination on real parts. The statewide picture, including Baton Rouge, Lake Charles and New Orleans, is on the NDT training in Louisiana page, and the US overview is on NDT training in the USA.

Training a crew at your Lafayette facility (employers)

A Lafayette inspection company or service shop that needs several people qualified at once can have them take the theory online, then complete hands-on training and practical examinations in person at its own yard, on its own equipment and parts. That keeps the specific and practical examinations tied to the work the crew really does, whether that is thread inspection, thickness surveys or weld examination.

Employers usually also need the paperwork to hold up. If your written practice was adapted from a template years ago, or no longer covers every method you use, written practice development brings it up to date, and outsourced ASNT Level III consulting can review procedures, build examinations and check certification files before an operator audit. Details on group training are on the corporate NDT training page.

Radiography licensing in Louisiana

Under its agreement with the NRC, Louisiana regulates radioactive materials itself. The Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, under Title 33, Part XV of the Louisiana Administrative Code, and it oversees the certification of industrial radiographers working in the state. A radiographer needs radiation safety training, supervised field experience as a trainee and the state-recognized radiographer certification, and must work under a company that holds a license.

An RT course teaches exposure technique and interpretation. It does not license anyone to handle a source. Most Lafayette radiographers need both: the radiation safety certification through their employer's licensed program and LDEQ, and SNT-TC-1A RT certification from their employer for the method itself. See radiographic testing training for the method course, and confirm current state requirements with LDEQ.

Practice before your practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser and lets you rehearse setups, coverage and interpretation before you stand in front of a real part. Lafayette trainees inspecting tubulars and fabrications get the most from the magnetic particle simulator, the UT simulator and the welding workshop. The simulator is practice; it does not count as logged experience and does not replace the practical examination.

For the written side, the free NDT practice tests cover each method, and the UT Level 2 practice questions are a good check before a general examination.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Lafayette

How long does it take to get NDT certified in Lafayette?

The written practice sets it. Theory hours can be finished in weeks if you study steadily, but supervised experience usually takes months, and that is what decides when your employer can certify you.

How much does NDT training cost in Lafayette?

The table on this page lists the published US fees for each course. Group training for a Lafayette employer is quoted on request through the contact form.

Can I do NDT training online in Louisiana?

Yes, for theory. The hands-on practical and the practical examination take place in person at the employer's facility.

Is there an NDT school near me in Lafayette?

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Lafayette or anywhere else in Louisiana. Theory is online, and the practical is done at your employer's site. Compare any local school on the questions listed above.

Which NDT method should I learn first for oilfield work?

VT and MT, because thread and connection inspection depends on them. Add UT next for thickness and lamination work.

Are there NDT jobs in Lafayette?

The oilfield service sector, tubular inspection yards, offshore fabricators, pipeline contractors and aviation maintenance all employ NDT technicians around Lafayette. Hiring follows drilling and offshore activity, so it rises and falls with the market.

Does my NDT certification transfer if I move to another Lafayette company?

Not automatically. Under SNT-TC-1A the new employer reviews your training, experience and examination records and certifies you under its own written practice. ASNT central certification travels with you.

Do I need ASNT Level 2 for tubular inspection?

Most operators expect the technician who interprets and accepts results to be Level II in the method, certified to the inspection company's written practice. Level I technicians work under that Level II.

Can I prepare for the ASNT Level III exams from Lafayette?

Yes. Level III preparation is self-paced on the portal with questions answered by the Level III. See ASNT Level III training.

Who teaches the courses?

Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with more than eleven years of international field experience, writes the courses and answers questions.
